See Church History Topics, “Joseph Smith Translation of the Bible,” Gospel Library; Kent P. Jackson, “How We Got the Book of Moses,”Religious Educator, vol. 3, no. 1 (2002), 127–38. While the book of Moses may include the restoration of material that was lost, it may also have been revelation given by the Lord to Joseph Smith that was never originally in the Bible. Either way, we do know that it restores many “plain and most precious” (1 Nephi 13:26) truths that Nephi foretold would be lost from the Bible (see1 Nephi 13:26–40).

See D. Todd Christofferson, “Choice and Commitment” (worldwide devotional for young adults, Jan. 12, 2020), Gospel Library. A third part of the spirit children of Heavenly Father followed Lucifer and rebelled against God and the plan of salvation, thereby failing to keep their first estate. They were therefore cast out of heaven, with no more opportunity to progress (seeJude 1:6;Revelation 12:7–9;Doctrine and Covenants 29:36).
